segments.text: Hi, I'm Shubhaa. This is my take-home for Legion Health: Texas patient onboarding, rebuilt to be AI-native. Here, onboarding ends when the first visit is completed, not when it's booked.

Today, of 5,898 sessions in thirty days, only 23.8 percent reach the payment page. Three steps lose 3,376 sessions: the conditions list, choosing a provider, and creating an account. And nothing is tracked after payment, so no one can see who completes a first visit.

Why now? Lifting start to payment from 24 to 30 percent means about 360 more patients a month reaching checkout, with no new acquisition spend. The data vendors are already live, but intake doesn't use them. And Rula and Grow book in minutes, with cost shown first.

So the solution is pull, then confirm, with a human in the loop. The patient gives a phone number, date of birth and one consent. We pull identity, insurance, records and medications in parallel, and the patient confirms instead of typing. If a pull fails, the patient simply answers. No second vendor.
That gives seven screens: the fewest where each screen does a single job. Safety stays separate, and every step is measurable, all the way to the first visit. Let me show it live.

segments.text: The patient enters a phone number and date of birth, gives one consent, and types a text code. That's almost all they'll type.

The key decisions follow one rule: one source per job. Verified only for identity, not Persona as well, to avoid cost, privacy exposure and conflicting data. Sohar for insurance, the only cost source shown. Metriport for records, in the background. DoseSpot for medications. And doubt always goes to a human.

Three trade-offs. Speed versus readiness. Book-first flows like Rula and Headway get people into a slot faster. I put safety and intake before booking, because the finish line is a completed first visit, not a booking. A slot taken by someone who needs a higher level of care, or who arrives with no history, is a wasted slot. Clicks versus safety. We pull insurance, meds and records at every step, but never use them silently. That costs a few clicks. In psychiatry a wrong medication history is a prescribing risk, so confirmation is the price of being AI-native safely. Conversion versus transparency. Showing the copay on screen 2 may lose some people early. Today they leave at step 11, after ten minutes. I'd rather they decide in thirty seconds. If completed visits per start don't rise, we revert.

The north star is start to first visit completed. Start to booked is the primary metric, because it moves first, and booked to visit completed is the guardrail, so faster booking doesn't create no-shows. Rollout is gated: we stop if safety or show rate slips.

How I built it. I used Claude to plan: the funnel analysis, research, the PRD and the designs. Claude Code then built the repo on GitHub, wrote tests that run in CI, deployed to Vercel, and opened the pull request, in about 43 minutes of autonomous work. I stayed in the loop throughout and made every product call.
Everything is linked here: the live prototype, the open pull request, the PRD, the designs and the full AI history. Thanks for watching.
